scope: Computational finite colored-tree certificate, plus the separate Lemma L2 construction tests described under l2_bank_orders. No claim of external peer review, formal verification, novelty, or authorship is supplied by this manifest.

changes: Resolve bundled inputs relative to supplement directory rather than repository parent.
Name the adapted verifier verify.py in generated provenance.
Default to a new verification-new.json instead of the frozen result name.
Reject Python optimization before any certificate processing; original assertion-based semantic checks retained.

Hardening of 9 November 2026 (after an agent mutation audit): require the certificate's input-binding list and the primary result's binding to name exactly the expected producer files, so an emptied list no longer passes; require integer types for colors, parents, arcs and active_arcs; assert the certificate's summary fields total_patterns, maximum_witness_arcs, direct_masks_examined and minimum_histogram against its records; count a negative control as rejected only on AssertionError.

Hardening of 14 November 2026 (after an outside AI audit of 13 November 2026 and a re-read of the first version of this hardening): read both JSON files with a hook that refuses a repeated key; require every value in the certificate outside the timing field, and in the counts, survivor list and histogram of the primary result, to be an integer, a string or null; require the status and schema strings to be the expected ones; require path records, and path survivors of the primary result, to carry no leg lengths and Y records three; require every direct_masks_examined to be non-negative; require identity_action, the edge-reflection action indices and the leaf-orbit action indices to lie in range(48); require minimum_histogram to equal that of the primary result, whose survivor list must have 80 entries.
adapted_consumer.semantic_changes: No change to domain enumeration, cube actions, witness replay, survivor checks, or the nine negative controls (seven semantic corruption controls and two set-comparison illustrations; wording corrected 2026-11-09, see README.md). The hardening of 9 November 2026 only adds assertions and narrows the exception type caught by the control wrapper; it accepts the shipped certificate with unchanged counts and rejects ten mutated inputs that the 5 November verifier accepted (see README.md, 'Hardening of 9 November 2026'). The hardening of 14 November 2026 again only adds assertions and a duplicate-key check on reading; it accepts the shipped certificate with unchanged counts and rejects 20 further altered inputs that the verifier of 9 November accepted (see README.md, 'Hardening of 14 November 2026').

l2_bank_orders.scope: Tests of the construction in the proof of Lemma L2 (manuscript Section 4.2). Not used by verify.py. Not a proof.
l2_bank_orders.origin: Written during the November 2026 correction of Section 4.2, previously kept as drafts/L2-supplement/. impl.py is adapted from impl_v2.py of the selected C_induction proof candidate, of which controls/C_induction_impl_v2.py is a byte copy: solve() and k2_cut() are unchanged apart from comments, docstrings and ProofGap message strings (the impl.py docstring, which says only "comments", is left as is); construct() tests (H1) and (H2) as stated in the final text and raises the recursion limit. l2harness.py is a byte copy of the shared test harness used to evaluate the candidates (sha256 d936b4d5c07831aa4545ace720f92adeb16c9aef1b345b0c0ebc7b3a87689489). The candidates' working files were in a temporary session directory and are not part of this package.
